class.name: AmbientProbeVolume3D
class.brief_description: Fills a box volume with a regular grid of [LightmapProbe] children, for large-scale baked ambient occlusion and indirect light.
class.description: [AmbientProbeVolume3D] automates placing many [LightmapProbe] nodes across a large area, instead of positioning each one by hand. Pressing the [b]Generate Probes[/b] button in the Inspector (or calling [method generate_probes]) fills the box defined by [member size] (centered on the node's origin) with a uniform grid of [member probe_counts] probes, added as child [LightmapProbe] nodes. The probes themselves store no data until a [LightmapGI] node bakes the scene: baking computes indirect light and ambient occlusion at every probe position (accounting for occluding static geometry), exactly like any other [LightmapProbe]. This is what makes the effect "large-scale": once baked, the probes have zero per-frame cost beyond a cheap trilinear lookup, so they scale to open scenes far larger than what [VoxelGI] can comfortably cover (see below), and can be regenerated over any area at any density without affecting the rest of the scene's baked lightmaps. This is intended for shading things that don't carry their own lightmap UVs, such as vegetation: a [MultiMeshInstance3D] full of grass or a [FoliageSpawner3D] can read the nearest baked probes for a plausible ambient term. For any [GeometryInstance3D] to actually sample these probes, its [member GeometryInstance3D.gi_mode] must be set to [constant GeometryInstance3D.GI_MODE_DYNAMIC]. Conversely, to make a mesh [i]not[/i] receive light from these (or any other baked) probes, e.g. for small objects like individual grass blades where the difference is not worth the lookup cost, set [member GeometryInstance3D.gi_mode] to [constant GeometryInstance3D.GI_MODE_DISABLED]; [FoliageSpawner3D] already does this by default. [b]VoxelGI vs. baked probes for large-scale ambient occlusion:[/b] [VoxelGI] voxelizes one fixed-resolution 3D texture (up to 256 per axis) across its whole box and updates in real time, which makes it a poor fit for very large or open outdoor areas: covering more world space either coarsens every voxel or spends a lot of GPU memory and bake/update time on a single volume, and its effect fades out near the box's edges. [LightmapProbe]/[LightmapGI] probes have no such resolution-vs-coverage trade-off (probes are just points, placed wherever needed, at whatever spacing is useful) and cost nothing at runtime once baked, at the expense of not reacting to moving lights or geometry. For large, mostly-static outdoor scenes, prefer a sparse grid of baked probes (this node) for ambient occlusion/indirect light on vegetation and other dynamic-GI objects; reserve [VoxelGI] for smaller, bounded areas (e.g. a single interior or a gameplay-relevant room) where real-time reaction to moving lights matters. [SDFGI] (via [member Environment.sdfgi_enabled]) is usually a better real-time alternative to [VoxelGI] for large open worlds, since it works from cascades around the camera instead of a single fixed volume, but still costs GPU time every frame that baked probes do not. [b]Note:[/b] Regenerating clears and replaces only the [LightmapProbe] nodes this node previously generated (tracked internally); manually added child nodes are left untouched. [method generate_probes] requires the node to already be part of a saved scene, since the generated probes need an owner to be saved and picked up by [LightmapGI].

method.name: clear_probes
method.description: Removes all [LightmapProbe] child nodes previously created by [method generate_probes]. Manually added [LightmapProbe] children are left untouched.

method.name: generate_probes
method.description: Clears any previously generated probes (see [method clear_probes]) and creates a new uniform grid of [member probe_counts] [LightmapProbe] child nodes filling [member size]. This only places the probes; bake a [LightmapGI] node afterwards to actually compute their ambient light and occlusion data.

method.name: get_generated_probe_count
method.description: Returns how many of this node's current children were generated by [method generate_probes] (as opposed to added manually).

members.member: Pressing this button in the Inspector calls [method clear_probes]. It is not meant to be read or assigned from code; use [method clear_probes] directly instead.
Pressing this button in the Inspector calls [method generate_probes]. It is not meant to be read or assigned from code; use [method generate_probes] directly instead.

The number of probes to generate along each axis, clamped between [code]1[/code] and [code]64[/code] per axis. The total probe count ([member probe_counts].x × [member probe_counts].y × [member probe_counts].z) directly affects [LightmapGI] bake time and the runtime cost of finding nearby probes, so keep it as low as the desired detail allows.
The size of the box volume that probes are generated within, centered on the node's origin.
